big_idea: We can GIVE and FOLLOW directions to move from one place to another.
learning_intention: We are learning to give and follow directions.
student_learning_goal: I can give and follow directions to move.
success_criteria: I can WRITE clear directions: forward, backward, left, right.
I can FOLLOW a partner's directions to find a treasure.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Tig and Coco — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
All previous manipulatives at 5 capstone stations
Lesson 5 capstone rubric — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Coco: I'll tell you how to find the treasure! Forward 3, turn right, forward 2. FOLLOW me! Tig opens: 'Map it, MOVE it!' Coco: 'Verb plus NUMBER!' Class: 'every TIME!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Tig and Coco puppets. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use ALL we know: SORT, BUILD, MATCH, LOCATE, MOVE!'

Introduce vocabulary. Write DIRECTION on chart. 'Direction = an instruction to MOVE — like "forward 3 steps" or "turn right".'

Demonstrate. Stand on a marked square on the floor. 'I will follow Coco's directions to find the treasure.'

Coco: 'Forward 2. Turn right. Forward 3.' Walk it out. 'There's the treasure!'

More examples. Children give teacher 3-step directions to walk to the door. Teacher follows.

Now the 5 capstone stations:
- Station 1: SORT — sort 8 shapes by attribute.
- Station 2: BUILD — build a 3-block structure, find shapes inside.
- Station 3: MATCH — fold 3 shapes, mark matching halves.
- Station 4: LOCATE — describe 3 locations on a map with position words.
- Station 5: MOVE — write 3-step directions on the trail map. Partner follows.

Each station: child completes ONE task on their CAPSTONE TEMPLATE.

'Tig says — every detective needs ALL 5 skills. Today YOU prove you have them.'

'Welcome to the TREASURE TRAIL!'
student_actions: Plan which station to start at.

steps.instruction: RECAP (5 min): Tig + Coco model each skill on the carpet — SORT, BUILD, MATCH, LOCATE — one quick example per skill.
steps.teacher_prompt: Tig + Coco: 'You can SORT, BUILD, MATCH, and LOCATE. Today you DIRECT a partner.'

steps.instruction:
STATIONS (20 min): children rotate through 4 capstone stations and record on the template.
  DIRECT: walk treasure trail with a partner.
  BUILD: sketch 2D shapes inside a 3-block structure.
  MATCH: fold a triangle and rectangle; mark symmetry lines.
  LOCATE: write 3 position-word sentences about a map.

differentiation.for_emerging: Visit Stations 1, 2, 5 only. Skip the trickier Match and Locate.
differentiation.for_extending: After all 5 stations, write a 'big conclusion' about what you learned.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide picture-cued sentence frames for each station.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between 5 station tables; physically engage at each. NO-PAPER VERSION: child gives 3 verbal directions to walk a partner from carpet edge to door; teacher records on a clipboard checklist instead of the capstone template.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: sorts; builds; matches; locates; gives directions.

discussion_prompts: How do you describe where something is?
consolidation.exit_routine: Tig + Coco — Tig: 'Map it, MOVE it!' Coco: 'Verb + NUMBER!' Class: 'every TIME!' Repeat 3x. Each child shares one direction fix.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures E1.5 (directions) AND reinforces E1.1-E1.4 in one capstone.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child gives directions only from their own viewpoint — repairing egocentric spatial reference
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the capstone where children give a partner directions to walk a treasure trail, the dominant Grade-1 trap is egocentric spatial reference — the child says 'go RIGHT' assuming the partner faces the SAME way the child does, then is surprised when partner walks left. Clements & Sarama (2009) place coordinated frames of reference as the gateway to mature spatial orientation; Piaget's three-mountains task is the classic decentre-required test.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: NAME attributes (L1), BUILD 3D structures (L2), MATCH halves/symmetry (L3), use POSITION vocabulary (L4) into a single direction-giving and -following task.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair stands at start of treasure trail. Partner is blindfolded. Child gives directions to walk to the treasure. Child says 'go RIGHT' but partner walks LEFT (because partner was facing the child).
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You said RIGHT, but Coco the partner walked LEFT. Why?'

Walk the child to partner's position, face partner's direction. 'From HERE, your right is partner's right. From OVER THERE, your right is partner's LEFT. Math directions need the LISTENER'S point of view.'

Drill verb + number: 'walk FORWARD 3 steps. Turn LEFT 1 quarter turn. Walk FORWARD 2.' Force every direction to have a NUMBER.

Coco's refrain — 'Verb plus NUMBER!' / 'every TIME!'

Long-term recovery: every direction is a verb + number pair, given from the listener's vantage.
expected_student_responses: (Confused) Says 'go right' from own perspective; partner walks wrong way.
(Mid) Adjusts after one error; uses verb + number pairs after coaching.
(Strong) Stands at partner's start, faces partner's way, then issues each direction.
(Stretched) Plans the whole sequence in the listener's frame before speaking.
common_misconceptions: Egocentric reference: 'go right' = my right, not yours. (Repair: stand at listener's start.)
Verb-without-number: 'walk forward' (how far?). (Repair: every verb gets a step count.)
Skips the turn: 'walk forward, walk forward' across a corner. (Repair: name the turn between segments.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child gestures only (points without speaking): force partner to face AWAY; child must use words.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child uses verbs without numbers: drill verb+number pairs ('forward 3', 'left turn 1'); child re-issues every direction in this format.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child uses own viewpoint: walk child to partner's start, face partner's way, then issue directions.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Summative artifact applying E1.1-E1.5 in 5 mini-tasks.
